 These Criminal Petitions, Coming On For Orders, This
Day, The Court Made The Following:
 Order

The petitioners-accused No.2 and 3 are before this Court seeking grant of anticipatory bail in Crime No.116/2024 of Jayanagar Police Station, pending on the file of the learned II Additional CMM Court, Nrupatunga Road, Bangalore City NC: 2024:KHC:20342 registered for the offences punishable under Sections 419, 420, 467, 468, 471 R/w Section 34 of Indian Penal Code (for short 'IPC'), on the basis of the first information lodged by the informant Prakash H.N.
2.
Heard Sri. Chandan Sanjay Bhat and Sri. Manjunath H., learned counsels for the petitioners and Sri.Rahul Rai K., learned High Court Government Pleader for the respondent- State.
Perused the materials on record.

3. In view of the rival contentions urged by the learned counsel for both the parties, the point that would arise for my consideration is:

sentences.text: "Whether the petitioners are entitled for grant of bail under Section 438 of Cr.P.C.?"

My answer to the above point is in 'Affirmative' for the following:
REASONS 4.
The informant lodged the first information making serious allegations against accused Nos.1 to 3 and unknown accused.

It is alleged that accused Nos.1 to 3 introduced one person as Zacharia Varghese to the informant and projected NC: 2024:KHC:20342 him as owner of the property,
shown by them.
They induced the complainant to purchase the same for a sum of Rs.1 Crore.

A sale agreement dated 22.04.2022 said to have been executed by the said person Zacharia Varghese in favour of the complainant, to which, accused No.1 had signed as consenting witness and these petitioners as witnesses.
It is stated that entire sale consideration of Rs.1 crore was paid under the registered sale agreement which was registered before the Sub-Registrar office of Jayanagar.
The amount was transferred through online.
It is stated that these petitioners demanded Rs.25 lakhs as their commission and received the same.
Thereafter, the complainant came to know that there is impersonation of executant of the agreement, as the original owner is the resident of America.
On these allegations, FIR came to be registered.
5. Admittedly, accused No.1 is already granted anticipatory bail by the Co-Ordinate Bench of this Court.
The same was never challenged by the prosecution or by the complainant.
On perusal of the first information, similar allegations are made and all the accused Nos.1 to 3 are signatories to the sale agreement.
The other person, who NC: 2024:KHC:20342 impersonated himself as Zacharia Varghese is shown as unknown accused.

6. Even though, serious allegations are made against these petitioners, that they have obtained Rs.25 lakhs as commission, the same was willingly paid by the complainant but without knowing about impersonation.
Regarding other allegations, similar allegations are made against accused Nos1 to 3.
When accused No.1 is granted anticipatory bail, I am of the opinion that these petitioners are also entitled for benefit of parity.
If the investigating officer deems it necessary to subject the petitioners for custodial interrogation, he is at liberty to do so with permission from the jurisdictional Magistrate.
Hence, I am of the opinion that the petitioners may be granted anticipatory bail subject to conditions, which will take care of the interest of the prosecution.

7. Accordingly, I answer the above point in the affirmative and proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The Crl.P.No.4094/2024 and Crl.P.No.4126/2024 are allowed.
NC: 2024:KHC:20342 The petitioners are ordered to be enlarged on bail in the event of their arrest in Crime No.116/2024 of Jayanagar Police Station.

The petitioners are directed to appear before the Investigating Officer within 15 days from the date of receipt of this order and on their appearance, the Investigating Officer shall enlarge them on bail subject to the following conditions:-

b.

c.

e. If in case, the Investigating officer deems necessary for subjecting the petitioners for custodial interrogation, he is at liberty to do so prior with prior permission from the jurisdictional Magistrate.
On furnishing the sureties by the petitioners, the Investigating Officer is at liberty to verify the correctness of the address and authenticity of the documents furnished by them.
